attacks.claim: The success target is not supported by the prototype. The prototype projected p75 LCP of 2.6 s, which is above the 2.5 s target, and it was a lab WebPageTest run on 50 articles, not field data. The 2.5 s field target is presented as achievable without a field or RUM projection.
attacks.evidence: WebPageTest (Moto G Power, 4G, 3 runs per article): p75 LCP 3.9 s → 2.6 s ... CrUX p75 mobile LCP on article pages ≤ 2.5 s within 6 weeks of 100%

attacks.claim: The gating flag can be set before all derivative objects exist, or can stay set after a partial write. A `<picture>` `<source>` pointing at a missing AVIF or WebP key produces a broken image, because browsers do not fall back to the next source on a network failure. The plan does not say the flag is set atomically after all uploads succeed, nor how a partial set left by a failed attempt is cleaned up before retry.
attacks.evidence: `` is rendered only when `image.has_responsive_set` is true (set by the task) ... make_responsive_set failures (3 retries, then alert to #web-alerts; the page keeps the plain ``)

attacks.claim: The 0.9 s per-image figure is a prototype average. Images can be up to 40 megapixels, and AVIF encoding at q50 on those sizes can take far longer and use much more memory. No per-task timeout, memory cap, or tail-latency bound is stated, so a few large images can stall workers and push the backfill past its window.
attacks.evidence: Throughput: 0.9 s per image for the full set (prototype, c6i.xlarge) ... the existing upload validation (JPEG/PNG/WebP/HEIC only, 40-megapixel limit)

attacks.claim: The backfill schedule has almost no margin and rests on unverified assumptions. About 9.7 h of work must fit in two 5 h windows (10 h), on worker nodes whose type is not stated, using a benchmark from a different instance type. The claim that publishing is 'never delayed' is not backed by any CPU or worker-pool isolation, since the low-priority queue runs on the same existing nodes.
attacks.evidence: Two existing worker nodes × 4 workers ≈ 9.7 h, run over two nights (01:00–06:00) on a separate low-priority Celery queue, so publishing tasks are never delayed.

attacks.claim: The plan asserts that wire-service licences cover new formats and sizes, but it does not quote the licence terms. Wire licences often restrict alteration, storage copies, and removal of credit metadata. The plan also strips all metadata, which may remove the IPTC credit lines those licences require.
attacks.evidence: Extra sizes and formats of the same licensed image for the same display use are covered by the current licences (photo desk confirmation on WEB-778, Oct 19)

attacks.claim: The srcset candidates are inconsistent across formats. AVIF and WebP offer 1600 px candidates, but the JPEG srcset stops at 1200 px, so browsers without AVIF or WebP get lower quality on 2x desktop. The JPEG `src` at 1600 px has no width descriptor and sits outside the srcset.
attacks.evidence: `` with the JPEG `srcset`; `src` is the existing 1600 px JPEG ... AVIF (q 50) and WebP (q 75) at 480/800/1200/1600 px

attacks.claim: The cost model leaves out per-request charges and assumes the CloudFront saving applies to all image egress. About 11 PUTs per image across 310,000 backfilled images is a one-time request cost that is not counted. The ~$1,000/month saving extrapolates an 800 px AVIF result from article lead images to all image traffic.
attacks.evidence: projected ~9 TB by applying the prototype's byte savings to September's traffic mix, ≈ $1,000/month less. This is an estimate

attacks.claim: Output quality is not validated. Format quality settings (AVIF q50, WebP q75) were chosen without a visual or perceptual check on text-heavy or high-detail news photos, and the prototype covered only 50 articles.
attacks.evidence: AVIF (q 50) and WebP (q 75) ... Prototype (WEB-771) on 50 recent articles

attacks.claim: The plan does not say how the 'validated type' is determined (magic bytes or extension). The HEIC decode path through libheif is a high-risk parser, and libvips 8.14 depends on Debian backports for security fixes, with no stated scanning or pinning.
attacks.evidence: the existing upload validation (JPEG/PNG/WebP/HEIC only, 40-megapixel limit) runs before either task ... security updates via unattended-upgrades

attacks.claim: The page switches to `<picture>` on `has_responsive_set`, but the plan never says the flag is set only after all 11 derivative keys are written and verified. A partial write or a failed retry could leave the flag true with missing candidates, and browsers do not fall back to another source on a 404, so the image breaks on live pages.
attacks.evidence: "`<picture>` is rendered only when `image.has_responsive_set` is true (set by the task)" / ABSENT: completeness check before flag, cleanup of partial keys on retry, and a rule for what happens if a single key 404s.

attacks.claim: A legal takedown can be undone by an in-flight or retrying `make_responsive_set` task that writes new derivatives after `purge_image` has run. The purge test only covers an image that already has a complete set, so this race is untested.
attacks.evidence: "Kill notices and legal takedowns use the `purge_image` management command" and "3 retries, then alert" / ABSENT: ordering or locking between purge and the derivative task, a takedown tombstone checked before writes, and a test that purges during generation.

attacks.claim: Wire-photo coverage for re-encoding, new formats and extra sizes rests on an internal ticket note, not on licence terms. Wire agency licences often restrict alteration, so the backfill of wire images could breach contract.
attacks.evidence: "covered by the current licences (photo desk confirmation on WEB-778, Oct 19)" / ABSENT: the licence clause text, or a reference to the specific agency terms permitting derivative creation.

attacks.claim: The success target is not supported by the prototype. The prototype reaches 2.6 s, which is above the 2.5 s target, and it is based on 50 articles with no variance or confidence interval. The 3.9 s lab baseline also matches the CrUX field figure exactly, which suggests lab and field numbers may be mixed.
attacks.evidence: "p75 LCP 3.9 s → 2.6 s" vs "CrUX p75 mobile LCP on article pages ≤ 2.5 s within 6 weeks of 100%" / ABSENT: evidence that the change reaches ≤2.5 s, and a same-method baseline.

attacks.claim: The plan relies on `VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED=1` as a control on libvips 8.14, but it does not show that this version honours the variable. HEIC is also accepted, which means libheif parses staff-uploaded files, and the worker's S3 permissions are not scoped.
attacks.evidence: "libvips 8.14 from the Debian 12 package" and "workers run with `VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED=1`" / ABSENT: a test showing the variable blocks the intended operations on 8.14, sandboxing for HEIC decoding, and the worker IAM policy.

attacks.claim: Backfill throughput depends on a 0.9 s/image figure from a 50-article prototype on c6i.xlarge, but the existing worker node type is not given. The 9.7 h estimate leaves almost no slack in the 10 h window before retries.
attacks.evidence: "0.9 s per image for the full set (prototype, c6i.xlarge)" and "≈ 9.7 h, run over two nights (01:00–06:00)" / ABSENT: benchmark on the actual nodes, and a plan for overrun or retries.

attacks.claim: The "~1 s" fallback window for live uploads is not benchmarked at the 40-megapixel limit or under queue backlog. The live task shares a default queue with publishing, so the window could be much longer during breaking news.
attacks.evidence: "an article published before its derivatives exist (~1 s) simply falls back" / ABSENT: timings for large originals and under load, and the queue the task uses.

attacks.claim: The JPEG `srcset` stops at 1200 px while AVIF and WebP go to 1600 px. Browsers without AVIF or WebP on high-DPR desktops would get 1200 px instead of today's 1600 px, a quality regression for that group.
attacks.evidence: "`` with the JPEG `srcset`; `src` is the existing 1600 px JPEG" and "JPEG at 480/800/1200 px"

attacks.claim: The CLS success measure allows a regression. A p75 ceiling of 0.05 against a 0.04 baseline permits a 25% increase while being labelled "no regression".
attacks.evidence: "No CLS regression: p75 ≤ 0.05 (today 0.04)"

attacks.claim: The storage forecast and backfill scope do not obviously reconcile. At ~9,000 uploads per month, 24 months gives about 216,000 uploads, yet 310,000 images in the 24-month article window are in scope.
attacks.evidence: "310,000 of 1.27M" and "~3 GB/month for ~9,000 new uploads" / ABSENT: an explanation of how the in-scope count relates to the upload rate.

attacks.claim: The cost model omits request charges. Each image adds 11 objects, which means roughly 3.4M PUTs for the backfill and extra CloudFront request charges per page view.
attacks.evidence: "≈ $2.50/month" and "CloudFront image egress" / ABSENT: PUT, GET and CloudFront request pricing for the new objects and URLs.

attacks.claim: The $1,000/month savings uses the prototype's 800 px byte figures, but mobile devices at 2–3x DPR will often select the 1200 px candidate, so the savings basis does not match what is served.
attacks.evidence: "800 px AVIF median 61 KB" and "applying the prototype's byte savings to September's traffic mix, ≈ $1,000/month less" / ABSENT: the price tier used and the size distribution that browsers actually request.

attacks.claim: The purge test checks only keys under the `<id>-` prefix. The plan does not say whether the original file's key matches that prefix, so the zero-keys assertion could pass while the original survives.
attacks.evidence: "delete every key under the image's `<id>-` prefix" and "assert zero remaining keys" / ABSENT: the original object's key format and an explicit assertion that it is deleted.

attacks.claim: The success criterion is not supported by the plan's own prototype. The prototype reaches p75 LCP 2.6 s, which is above the 2.5 s target, and the plan has no step that closes the 0.1 s gap.
attacks.evidence: WebPageTest ... p75 LCP 3.9 s → 2.6 s ... CrUX p75 mobile LCP on article pages ≤ 2.5 s within 6 weeks of 100%

attacks.claim: The headline improvement compares a field CrUX baseline with a lab WebPageTest result from 50 articles x 3 runs on one device profile. These measurements are not comparable, so the 3.9 s to 2.6 s delta cannot be read as a field improvement.
attacks.evidence: Chrome UX Report, September: p75 mobile LCP on article pages is 3.9 s ... WebPageTest (Moto G Power, 4G, 3 runs per article): p75 LCP 3.9 s → 2.6 s

attacks.claim: Wire-licence coverage for new formats and re-encodes is asserted on a photo-desk confirmation. No licence-terms or legal review is cited, and wire licences often restrict alteration and derivative works.
attacks.evidence: Extra sizes and formats of the same licensed image for the same display use are covered by the current licences (photo desk confirmation on WEB-778, Oct 19).

attacks.claim: Queue separation does not isolate CPU. The backfill shares the same worker nodes that run publishing tasks, with 4 workers per 4-vCPU node, so low-priority work can delay publishing. The claim that publishing is never delayed is unsupported.
attacks.evidence: run over two nights (01:00–06:00) on a separate low-priority Celery queue, so publishing tasks are never delayed ... Two existing worker nodes × 4 workers

attacks.claim: The backfill estimate leaves no slack. About 9.7 h of work must fit in a 10 h window with no retry budget or stop/resume plan for overruns.
attacks.evidence: ≈ 9.7 h, run over two nights (01:00–06:00)

attacks.claim: The takedown procedure only targets one image id. The plan does not say how it finds sibling ids derived from the same original photo, even though re-crops create new ids, so a takedown can leave a copy live.
attacks.evidence: Re-crops already create a new image id (new keys) ... purge_image ... delete every key under the image's <id>- prefix

attacks.claim: The JPEG srcset stops at 1200 px while src is 1600 px. Browsers that honour srcset ignore src, so the JPEG fallback is capped at 1200 px even though the 1600 px file exists.
attacks.evidence: an with the JPEG srcset; src is the existing 1600 px JPEG ... JPEG at 480/800/1200 px

attacks.claim: The 340 KB per-image storage figure and the 9 TB egress projection rest on prototype data measured only at 800 px. The 1200 and 1600 px AVIF/WebP sizes, which serve desktop and high-DPR traffic, are unmeasured.
attacks.evidence: prototype ... 800 px AVIF median 61 KB, WebP 88 KB ... projected ~9 TB by applying the prototype's byte savings

attacks.claim: The plan treats authenticated staff uploads as trusted-origin. Staff upload untrusted third-party files, and the plan gives no evidence that VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED covers the HEIC decode path. It also sets no per-task time or memory limits.
attacks.evidence: Uploads come only from authenticated CMS staff ... workers run with VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED=1

attacks.claim: width and height are taken from stored dimensions, which may be the original rather than the post-crop output. A mismatch would distort the image or cause layout shift, against the CLS target.
attacks.evidence: gains width/height from stored dimensions to prevent layout shift

attacks.claim: The largest srcset candidate is 1600 px, but a 720 CSS px column on a 3x device needs about 2160 px. Retina lead images will be upscaled, and the plan does not address this.
attacks.evidence: sizes="(max-width: 720px) 100vw, 720px" ... AVIF and WebP at 480/800/1200/1600 px

attacks.claim: The rollout compares RUM groups on a 5% sample, with no sample-size target, statistical threshold, or automatic stop criterion at each 10%→50%→100% step.
attacks.evidence: comparing RUM LCP and CLS between groups at each step
